key_insight: High-velocity air fuel (HVAF) spraying can produce thick NiTi shape-memory coatings that retain martensitic transformation and functional response after annealing, despite heterogeneous microstructure.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical path to add self-actuating, wear-resistant NiTi surfaces to engineering components where conventional ceramic or plating routes are unsuitable.
method: HVAF sprayed NiTi onto mild steel using four processing parameter sets
Characterized composition, porosity, microstructure, phase transformation, and thermomechanical behavior
Post-spray annealing was used to recover functional shape-memory properties
evidence_signal: The coatings were evaluated by microstructural and phase analyses plus bending, nanoindentation, and scratch tests, which showed martensitic transformation and thermal actuation/shape-memory behavior.
watch_item: As-sprayed coatings were heterogeneous and defect-rich, so annealing and careful process control are critical to achieve reliable functional performance.
paper_title: HVAF Spraying of NiTi Coatings: Microstructure, Phase Transformation and Shape Memory Behavior
